_comment: Where ground vehicles go, see wilcoatc/atc/servicelayout.py. 'roles': which door each vehicle serves is chosen from the aeroplane's own interactive points; standoff_m is how far out from the door along the way it faces, along_m how far forward along the fuselage, facing 'door' (nose to the door), 'away' (backed up to it) or a heading relative to the aeroplane. 'vehicles': per simulator title, the model's own correction in its own frame (right_m, forward_m, heading_deg) -- written by scripts/place_vehicle.py. 'types': per ICAO type, [right, forward, heading] in metres for a role whose door the model does not report. Defaults derived from the hand-calibrated spots against the flyable A321's measured doors (stairs 3.6 m out of L1, caterer 3.1 m out of R1, loader 4.9 m out of the hold). 'sill_below_point_m': how far a door's sill is below its interactive point, by kind (zero: markers on the flyable A321 sat on the floor of each open door, Bilbao 17 October). 'loaders': per belt-loader title, the belt from the model's own cfg (GSX's Tug 660 [BaggageLoader]: pivot and flat end as up/forward from the origin, and the animation's MAX_ANGLE), which docks the loader by its belt: belt_gap_m is how far short of the hold point the raised belt's end stops. 'stairs_models': GSX's staircases, best first, from each one's own sim.cfg [Couatl]: the platform floor's height (= BOARDINGRAMP ELEVATION, its model's BASE_HEIGHT..MAX_HEIGHT) and how far ahead of the origin the platform's front edge is at that height ('extension'), and 'fits', the door sills GSX itself uses it for ('condition' on exitAlt). A passenger door gets the first listed one that fits its sill, else 'stairs_fallback'; stairs_gap_m is how far the platform's front edge stops from the door point.
